summary: Describes MGCP, a protocol for controlling Voice over IP gateways from external call control elements. The call control intelligence lives outside the gateways, which simply follow instructions. This is an informational memo, and it was replaced by RFC 3435.

eli5.summary: The gateway is like a puppet and a separate controller pulls the strings. The controller decides what happens in each phone call.

questions: how do call agents control voip gateways
what is the difference between mgcp and sip
subtitle: A master/slave protocol where an external call agent tells VoIP gateways which connections to create, change and delete.

tldr.problem: Telephony gateways convert between phone-circuit audio and IP packets, and putting call-control intelligence inside every gateway makes them complex and hard to coordinate.
tldr.mechanism: MGCP moves the intelligence into external Call Agents. They send short text commands over UDP to create, modify, delete and audit connections on gateway endpoints and to request event notifications, and the gateways simply execute them.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2705 is an Informational memo, and it has been replaced by RFC 3435, which obsoletes it, and later updated by RFC 3660.

today: RFC 2705 is an Informational memo, not a standard. It has been obsoleted by RFC 3435 and updated by RFC 3660, so read RFC 3435 for the current MGCP specification.

sections.title: Gateways and Call Agents
sections.content:
RFC 2705 describes an abstract application programming interface and a protocol, the Media Gateway Control Protocol (MGCP), for controlling telephony gateways from external call control elements called Call Agents (or media gateway controllers). A telephony gateway converts between audio signals on telephone circuits and data packets on the Internet or other packet networks. The RFC lists trunking, Voice over ATM, residential, access and business gateways, network access servers, and circuit or packet switches.

MGCP is, in essence, a master/slave protocol. The gateways are expected to execute commands sent by the Call Agents, so the RFC specifies the gateway's behavior in great detail but only those parts of a Call Agent, such as timer management, that are needed for proper operation. MGCP does not define how Call Agents synchronize with each other.

An IESG note says the protocol was being deployed in a number of products, and that implementers should watch the IETF Megaco Working Group and ITU-T SG16, who were working on a potential successor.
sections.eli5: A phone call between the old phone network and the Internet needs a translator box, the gateway. Instead of making each box smart, one smart boss tells all the boxes what to do.

sections.title: Endpoints, Connections and Calls
sections.content:
MGCP's model has two building blocks. Endpoints are sources or sinks of data, either physical (a trunk circuit to a phone switch, an analog line) or virtual (an audio source in an announcement server). Connections link endpoints, point to point or multipoint, over RTP and UDP on an IP network, over AAL2 on ATM, or over an internal connection inside a gateway.

An endpoint identifier has two parts: the domain name of the gateway and a local name, joined as local-name@domain. Local-name terms are separated by slashes, as in the example X35V3+A4/13 (an interface and a circuit number). An asterisk wildcard means all values and a dollar sign wildcard means any one value.

Each connection has a mode: sendonly, recvonly, sendrecv, confrnce, data, inactive, loopback, conttest, netwloop or netwtest. A Call Agent also assigns a call identifier, shared by all connections of one call, which is useful for accounting. Gateways create the connection identifiers.
sections.eli5: An endpoint is one phone socket on the box. A connection is a string between two sockets, and the mode says which way the sound can flow along that string.

sections.title: The Commands
sections.content:
The interface defines nine commands. The Call Agent can send EndpointConfiguration (line-side coding, for example A-law or mu-law), NotificationRequest (watch for events such as hook actions or DTMF tones), CreateConnection, ModifyConnection, DeleteConnection, AuditEndpoint and AuditConnection. The gateway sends Notify when requested events occur, RestartInProgress when it or a group of endpoints goes out of or back into service, and it can also send DeleteConnection when a connection cannot be sustained.

To connect two endpoints managed by the same Call Agent, three steps are used. The Call Agent asks the first gateway to create a connection, and gets back a session description (for example IP address, UDP port and packetization parameters). It passes that description in a CreateConnection to the second gateway, which answers with its own. A ModifyConnection then gives the second description to the first endpoint, and audio flows in both directions. If different Call Agents are involved, they synchronize through a call-agent to call-agent signaling protocol.

Session descriptions use the Session Description Protocol (SDP). Events and signals are grouped in packages, with names such as D (DTMF), M (MF), T (Trunk) and L (Line), and the RFC defines a set of basic packages. Experimental package names start with x-.
sections.eli5: The boss asks the first box to open a line and tell it how to reach it. The boss hands that address to the second box, then tells the first box how to reach the second. Now both can talk.

sections.title: Text Messages and UDP Transport
sections.content:
Messages are plain text lines. A command has a command line with four items (the verb, the transaction identifier, the endpoint name and the protocol version) followed by parameter lines. The verb is a four-letter code such as CRCX or DLCX. A transaction identifier is up to 9 decimal digits (0 to 999,999,999) and pairs a response with its command. Every command is acknowledged, and the response carries a return code: 100 to 199 are provisional, 200 to 299 success, 400 to 499 transient errors and 500 to 599 permanent errors.

MGCP runs over UDP. When no port is given, Call Agents send to port 2427 on gateways and gateways send to port 2727 on Call Agents. Because UDP can lose packets and most commands are not idempotent, entities keep a list of recent responses and in-progress transactions, so a repeated command is answered again rather than executed twice (at-most-once behavior). A suggested value for the long timer is 30 seconds.

The RFC deliberately gives no fixed retransmission timer. It suggests estimating the delay as TCP does, doubling after each retransmission with a random component, and bounding the timer (a suggested maximum is 4 seconds). A provisional response with code 100 tells the sender a slow transaction is still running. Several messages may share one UDP packet, separated by a line holding a single dot.
sections.eli5: The boss and the boxes send each other short typed notes. Each note has a number so replies match the right question, and if a reply does not arrive the note is sent again, but a box never does the same job twice.

sections.title: Failover, Races and Security
sections.content:
Call Agents are named by domain name, and each endpoint has exactly one notified entity, the Call Agent currently controlling it, to which it sends its commands. A backup Call Agent can instruct endpoints to switch. If a Call Agent fails and no backup contacts them, its endpoints become disconnected. The RFC also covers a quarantine buffer for events that arrive while a notification is pending, ordering of commands, and a randomized procedure to avoid a restart avalanche.

For security, the RFC expects MGCP messages to always be carried over secure Internet connections using IP security, either the IP Authentication Header or the Encapsulating Security Payload. Gateways and Call Agents should accept only messages that IP security authenticated, and encryption protects against eavesdropping. This does not necessarily stop denial of service by misbehaving entities, but it identifies them.

For the audio itself, the RFC notes the risk of uncontrolled barge-in: packets sent to a connection's address and port get played on the line side. Checking source addresses slows call setup and can be fooled by spoofing, so it describes encrypting and authenticating the media with a secret key conveyed during call setup.
sections.eli5: Only the real boss should be able to give orders, so the notes are locked with a secret code. Otherwise a stranger could make calls or break in on a conversation.

sections.title: Where MGCP Came From
sections.content:
The RFC says MGCP resulted from combining two earlier proposals, SGCP and IPDC. The abstract describes the document's last part as the changes made in combining SGCP 1.1 and IPDC to create MGCP 1.0. Changes from SGCP include the formal wildcard naming of endpoints, the package structure for events, and new audit and restart operations (the audit commands were requested by CableLabs).

An appendix proposes a new MoveConnection command to move a connection from one endpoint to another on the same gateway, for services such as call forwarding. It is only a proposal.
sections.eli5: MGCP is what you get when two groups merged their ideas for how the boss should control the boxes into a single plan.

messages.label: CreateConnection
messages.note: Create a connection on the first endpoint.

messages.label: Response + session description
messages.note: Tells how to send packets to this connection.

messages.label: ModifyConnection
messages.note: Hands over the second description; audio flows both ways.

items.label: EndpointConfiguration
items.desc: Sets the line-side coding of an endpoint.

items.label: CreateConnection
items.desc: Creates a connection on an endpoint.

items.label: DeleteConnection
items.desc: Deletes a connection; a gateway can also send it.

items.label: NotificationRequest
items.desc: Asks the gateway to watch for events.

items.label: AuditEndpoint
items.desc: Reads the status of an endpoint.

items.label: AuditConnection
items.desc: Reads the status of a connection.

items.label: RestartInProgress
items.desc: Gateway signals endpoints leaving or returning to service.
